events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.
I’ll inspect the existing app and its conventions, then build the book list, detail page, and JSON-file persistence within that stack.

events.content: The workspace is a minimal Node project with no app yet. I’ll use Node’s built-in HTTP server and a small browser UI, so the app needs no database or new runtime dependencies.

args.content:
# Reading Room

A small personal bookshelf with no accounts or database. Books are stored in `data/books.json` and remain available after restarting the server.

## Run

```sh
npm install
npm start
```

Open http://localhost:3000. Set `PORT` to use another port. Use `npm run dev` for an auto-restarting development server.

## Checks

```sh
npm run build
npm test
```

Book pages have shareable URLs (`/books/<book-id>`). Anyone who can reach your server and has a book link can read its title, author, and notes; this app has no authentication. The `data/` folder is git-ignored to keep your personal books out of version control. Back up `data/books.json` if you want to retain your library when moving the app.
